descriptors.concept_name: Scope of Revenue from Contracts with Customers
descriptors.definition: Ind AS 115 applies to all contracts with customers to provide goods or services in the ordinary course of business for consideration. It excludes specific arrangements such as leases, insurance contracts, financial instruments, and certain non-monetary exchanges.
inclusion: Contracts with customers to provide goods or services as ordinary outputs
exclusion: Non-monetary exchanges between entities in the same line of business
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes transactions involving ordinary customers from collaboration arrangements where parties share risks and benefits.

descriptors.definition: This section sets out foundational terminology used throughout the revenue standard, including contracts, contract assets, contract liabilities, and performance obligations. These terms provide the technical definitions required to execute the five-step revenue recognition model.
inclusion: Standardized accounting definitions for revenue recognition mechanics
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between contract assets conditioned on factors other than the passage of time versus unconditional rights to consideration.

descriptors.definition: Ind AS 115 operates on a core principle requiring entities to recognize revenue depicting the transfer of goods or services at expected consideration amounts. This is implemented through a sequential five-step framework spanning contract identification, performance obligation determination, price determination, price allocation, and revenue recognition.
inclusion: Five sequential steps of revenue recognition
Full and modified retrospective transition approaches
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes the overarching five-step methodology from individual operational steps.

descriptors.definition: Entities apply Ind AS 115 either retrospectively or via a modified retrospective approach with cumulative effects recognized at initial application. The initial step requires identifying enforceable agreements with customers, which can be written, oral, or implied by customary business practices.
inclusion: Transition adjustment mechanics
Recognition of oral and implied contracts based on customary practices
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes full restatement of prior periods from cumulative-effect opening retained earnings adjustments.

descriptors.definition: Step 1 acts as a mandatory gateway requiring an entity to establish that an agreement creates legally enforceable rights and obligations. Entities must evaluate local legal environments to confirm enforceability before applying subsequent steps of the revenue model.
inclusion: Legal enforceability assessment
Evaluation of written, oral, or implied agreements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes preliminary negotiations lacking enforceability from binding contracts that pass the Step 1 gateway.

descriptors.definition: A contract is accounted for under Ind AS 115 only when approval, identification of rights, identification of payment terms, commercial substance, and probable collection of consideration are met. If these criteria fail at inception, no accounting contract exists and non-refundable consideration received is deferred.
inclusion: Five mandatory criteria for contract recognition
Deferral of non-refundable consideration when criteria are unmet
exclusion: Contracts meeting all criteria at inception requiring reassessment without significant factual changes
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes arrangements where collection is probable from high credit-risk arrangements failing initial contract criteria.

descriptors.concept_name: Contracts that do not pass Step 1 and Contract Term
descriptors.definition: Once a contract passes Step 1, existence is not reassessed unless significant facts and circumstances change adversely, such as a customer's credit deterioration. The contract term covers the period in which parties have present enforceable rights and obligations.
inclusion: Prospective impact analysis for subsequent collectibility failures
Contractual period definition
exclusion: Retrospective reversal of previously recognized revenues or receivables
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes prospective adjustments on remaining obligations from retrospective restatements of transferred goods.

descriptors.definition: A contract does not exist if each party can unilaterally terminate a wholly unperformed contract without penalty. Substantive termination penalties establish enforceable rights and obligations throughout the penalty period, determining the accounting contract term.
inclusion: Evaluation of cancellation clauses and cancellation penalties
Determination of enforceable contract duration
exclusion: Contracts with non-substantive termination penalties extending beyond cancellation dates
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes penalty-free cancellable periods from periods bound by substantive termination penalties.

descriptors.definition: Entities must combine two or more contracts entered into at or near the same time with the same customer if they share a commercial objective, pricing interdependence, or constitute a single performance obligation. Such arrangements are accounted for as a single contract to reflect their commercial substance.
inclusion: Aggregation of contracts with linked pricing or single commercial objectives
exclusion: Contracts negotiated simultaneously but serving independent commercial objectives with distinct performance obligations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes integrated packages requiring combined accounting from separate contracts executed concurrently.

descriptors.definition: A contract modification is an approved change in contract scope, price, or both. Modifications are accounted for either as separate distinct contracts, as a termination of the old contract and creation of a new one, or through cumulative catch-up adjustments.
inclusion: Identification of scope and price amendments
Separate contract treatment for distinct goods priced at stand-alone values
exclusion: Unapproved operational changes lacking legal enforceability
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes modifications treated as separate standalone contracts from those requiring cumulative catch-up adjustments.

descriptors.definition: Performance obligations serve as the fundamental unit of account in Ind AS 115, dictating when revenue is recognized. Entities must evaluate explicit promises as well as implicit commitments arising from customary business practices or published policies.
inclusion: Explicit contractual promises
Implicit promises creating valid customer expectations
exclusion: Administrative steps unrelated to transferring promised goods or services
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes explicit contract terms from implied obligations generated by established business policies.

descriptors.definition: At contract inception, entities assess all promised goods or services to identify distinct performance obligations. Promises can encompass manufactured goods, retail merchandise, consulting tasks, standby availability, asset construction, intellectual property licenses, or future purchase options.
inclusion: Evaluations of various promised outputs including tasks, licenses, and future options
exclusion: Activities that do not transfer a promised good or service to the customer
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes distinct promises evaluated as separate performance obligations from integrated components of a single combined promise.
